articles.title: Man City chairman confident club will prove innocence
articles.summary: Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak says he is still confident of proving the club's innocence after they were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.
body: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak says he is still confident of proving the club's innocence after they were found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules.

City were accused of a wide range of rule breaches, centring around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial regulations.
On Friday, it was announced City had been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges brought against them and Al Mubarak has responded with a letter to fans on the club's website.
"Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I," Al Mubarak said.

articles.title: Manchester City chairman Al Mubarak insists ‘nothing has changed’ after guilty verdict
articles.summary: Manager Maresca posts ‘I know nothing’ message. David Bernstein: a fine is not sufficient if appeal fails. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the Manchester City chair, has spoken for the first time since the club was found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules, saying…
body: News broke on Friday that City had been found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, charges the club have always strenuously denied.

The club did not comment on the verdict until Saturday afternoon when Al Mubarak took to social media, saying: “While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.

“We have some exciting moments to look forward to after this international break. We travel to Anfield in a fortnight, and then host Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League back at Etihad Stadium – moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the strength of the Manchester City family. Thank you, as always, for your constant support.”
Earlier, the cmanager, Enzo Maresca, posted a cryptic message on social media reading “I know nothing”.

articles.title: Ireland players vote to go ahead with Israel matches despite ‘different views’
articles.summary: Scheduled press conference and training session delayed. Irish FA admits ‘players shared different views’ The Republic of Ireland’s Nations League fixtures with Israel will go ahead after players voted on Saturday for the matches to be played.
body: The scheduled press conference before Sunday’s first game – which is being played in Debrecen in Hungary – was delayed until Saturday afternoon, raising doubts as to whether the match would be cancelled.

However, the Football Association of Ireland confirmed it will be played. “The Association made this decision following consultation with the Republic of Ireland players who shared different views and a majority expressed that the fixtures should be played. The Association respects the views of all players involved and appreciates the level of sensitivity concerning these fixtures.”

A group of players were believed to have held a meeting in the team hotel after missing the initial press conference, which was scheduled for 10.15am local time, and scheduled training at the Nagyerdei Stadium 45 minutes later.

articles.title: Norris says Colapinto should be banned after accident
articles.summary: World champion Lando Norris calls for Alpine's Franco Colapinto to be banned for causing an accident at a restart at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
body: McLaren's Norris was taken out in a chain reaction when the Argentine locked up his brakes and slid into team-mate Pierre Gasly, who then hit Norris. All three cars retired as a result of the incident.
Norris told BBC Radio 5 Live: "Give him a ban. It's quite simple."
Colapinto said: "I can be sorry to everyone. It's been a big mistake, of course. I just locked up and then I was very out of control."

Briton Norris said he believed governing body the FIA should take such incidents more seriously because of the impact it has on other drivers who are blameless, and the cost in terms of damaged parts.

As well as the intention to wear black armbands for Sunday's 'away' game against Israel in Debrecen, Courell said the players will make further gestures for the initial game and the return 'home' fixture against Israel next Sunday in Serbia.

articles.summary: The UNLV Rebels return from their bye week on Saturday when they travel to Ohio to take on the Akron Zips at InfoCision Stadium. How to Watch UNLV vs Akron. Date: Saturday, September 26, 2026. Time: 12:00 PM ET. Channel: ESPN+.
body: UNLV enters at 1-2 after a difficult 44-6 loss to North Texas snapped the program’s six-game winning streak against nonconference opponents. The Rebels have still been excellent away from home in recent seasons, winning 12 road games since the start of 2024, the most of any team in college football over that span. Saturday will also be UNLV’s third consecutive road game and its fourth different time zone through the opening month of the season.

Akron is also 1-2 after falling 41-7 at Minnesota last weekend, with its lone victory coming in a 45-10 home win over Robert Morris. This matchup has a unique bit of history, as the programs have met only once before. Akron defeated UNLV 27-6 in the 1976 NCAA Division II playoffs, meaning Saturday will end a 50-year gap between meetings.

articles.title: Man City chairman responds to reports surrounding 115 charges
articles.summary: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has reaffirmed his belief the club will prove their innocence in the Premier League 115 charges case following reports on Friday.
body: Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage, after reports claimed that most of the charges against the club for breaking Financial Fair Play rules were found to have been proven.
However, in a statement released on Saturday afternoon, the City chairman said "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

Describing his stance on the situation, Al Mubarak said in a message to City's supporters: "Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

articles.title: Klopp reacts to Karim Adeyemi’s horror miss vs Netherlands: ‘We are working with him’
articles.summary: Jurgen Klopp’s first match as manager of the German national team saw his side play out a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands, now coached by former Barcelona boss Xavi Hernandez. Germany were heading towards a narrow 1-0 victory until a late goal from Cody Gakpo.
body: In the first half, with Germany already leading 1-0, Adeyemi almost had an empty goal to aim at thanks to some smart play from Nathaniel Brown. But the forward failed to even hit the target.
Now, Jurgen Klopp has reacted to the Adeyemi miss for the first time as Germany prepare for their next game against Greece tomorrow.
The former Dortmund coach defended the former Dortmund player, adding that Adeyemi has enjoyed a solid start at Barcelona and he is delighted with what he brings to the table.
“The Karim I got to know here is a wonderful and very kind young man. And he’s left an excellent impression so far at Barcelona. Being here means a lot to him,” he said (h/t Sport1 ).

articles.title: Warwickshire win County Championship
articles.summary: Warwickshire thrashed visitors Leicestershire by an innings and 79 runs at Edgbaston to seal a ninth County Championship title and their first since 2021 on Saturday.
body: They entered the third day needing seven wickets to clinch the title, while the visitors needed 182 more runs to send them back in to bat.

Chris Woakes got the hosts off to the ideal start by bowling Sol Budinger for 47 and the former England all-rounder soon struck again when his delivery to Jonathan Tattersall was caught by Rob Yates at slip.

Leicestershire began to crumble as Ethan Bamber claimed the scalps of Ben Cox and Ben Green in quick succession and skipper Ian Holland was trapped lbw by Ed Barnard as the hosts closed in on the title.
Ajaz Patel was bowled by Manav Suthar, but Leicestershire dug in with a productive final-wicket partnership between Tom Scriven and Josh Hull.
